content.text: The document expressly disclaims any minimum commitment. This meets the preferred position.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets our preferred position: § 2.1 (p0013) states expressly that no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies, that Customer pays only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form, and that declining to place further orders is neither a breach nor a shortfall. This is reinforced by § 7.1 (p0026), which bars any minimum-use or similar charge not identified in the Order Form, and § 12.3 (p0051), in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. No take-or-pay, ratchet, or non-reducible volume obligation appears in the Order Form mechanics (§ 4) or renewal terms (§ 8) — § 8.2 in fact gives Customer a unilateral 30-day non-renewal right on each twelve-month Order Form period. The only "shortfall" references (§ 22, p0095–p0096) concern a licence-audit true-up for usage above entitlements, which is a true-up rather than a commitment penalty and is outside this rule. No redline required.
